monthly_review.summary: You've reduced volume but increased intensity this month, with faster average pace and higher HR zone distribution in Z3–Z4 — a clear shift toward more structured, threshold-focused work.
monthly_review.highlight: Your Zone 3–4 time jumped from 46% to 49% of total HR time — the largest shift across all zones — indicating intentional focus on lactate threshold development.

goal_tracker.message: You need 25.5 more km across 6 sessions in the remaining 19 days — averaging ~4.3 km/session — to match last month’s volume. Prioritize consistency: aim for one run every 3 days, including at least two runs ≥6 km.

insights.title: Improved efficiency despite slower long run
insights.body: Your aerobic efficiency rose to 13.64 m/sec per bpm (from 13.46), even though your longest run (14.1 km) was run at 9:22/km (562 sec/km) — notably slower than your best pace (6:32/km = 392 sec/km). This suggests better cardiovascular economy at lower intensities, likely due to improved stroke volume or capillarization.

insights.title: Overrepresentation of Zone 3–4 at expense of Z1–Z2 recovery
insights.body: Zone 3+ now accounts for 49% of HR time (Z3:26%, Z4:23%), up from 46% last month — while Z1+Z2 dropped from 43% to 41%. Your July 5 run (10.0 km @ 166 bpm, 4.0 TE) was likely Z4, but no Z1/Z2 runs occurred in the last 5 — risking insufficient recovery stimulus.

insights.title: Cadence-stride tradeoff evident in easy vs hard efforts
insights.body: Cadence dropped to 136 spm during your easiest run (July 8, 4.0 km @ 129 bpm), while stride length increased to 85.27 cm — suggesting overstriding at low effort. Conversely, your hardest run (July 5) maintained high cadence (154 spm) and stable stride (75.73 cm), aligning with efficient form under load.

insights.title: High TE density despite fewer runs
insights.body: Average aerobic TE rose to 3.0 (from 2.7) with 40% fewer runs — meaning each session delivered ~67% more aerobic stimulus. This is supported by elevated avg HR (+4 bpm) and 10% Z5 time (vs 1% last month), confirming acute loading — but requires careful recovery monitoring given only 1 Z1 run in recent history.

recommendations.action: Do a 5 km Zone 2 run (HR ≤135 bpm) on your next easy day, focusing on cadence ≥148 spm and avoiding overstriding (keep stride length ≤78 cm, as seen in your July 1 and July 12 runs).
recommendations.reason: Your recent easy runs show cadence dropping below 140 spm and stride length spiking above 85 cm — undermining efficiency gains. A dedicated Z2 session will rebuild aerobic base while reinforcing optimal turnover.

recommendations.action: Insert a 20-min post-run cooldown walk immediately after your next threshold session (e.g., after a Z3/Z4 run), keeping HR <115 bpm for full 20 minutes.
recommendations.reason: With zero Z1 time in your last 5 runs and only 16% Z1 in July overall, active cooldowns are critical to restore parasympathetic tone and offset accumulated Z3–Z4 load.

recommendations.action: Repeat your July 6 'recovery jog' (0.9 km @ 7:55/km, HR 137 bpm) as a standalone 1.0–1.2 km shakeout before your next long run — not as filler between workouts.
recommendations.reason: That short, low-HR run demonstrated ideal Z2 pacing (137 bpm ≈ 87% of your ~157 bpm estimated Z2 upper bound) and produced 2.0 TE — perfect for neuromuscular priming without fatigue.

weekly_focus.description: Prioritize frequency and physiological recovery over distance or intensity — use Z2 as the default for 3 of 5 weekly runs, embed cooldowns, and protect one true rest day.
suggested_sessions: 5 km Z2 run (HR ≤135 bpm, cadence ≥148 spm)
8 km mixed-effort run (first 4 km Z2, final 4 km Z3 @ 152–158 bpm)
